title: Junta and Arakan Army Resume Heavy Fighting Along Sittwe-Ponnagyun Border After Month-Long Lull
detail: Fighting broke out on the morning of September 4, 2026 along the Sittwe-Ponnagyun township border in Rakhine State, ending a roughly month-long lull in combat around the state capital. Regime forces deployed heavy artillery, multiple-launch rocket systems (MLRS) and combat drones from positions including the Shwe Min Gan naval base area, while the Arakan Army (AA) returned fire with artillery, drones and small-arms. Shells landed in Kuntaung, Padetha and Yarchaung villages and in Ponnagyun town itself; a woman was injured on September 4. Thousands of residents fled Ponnagyun and Rathedaung townships — including the villages of Tabethlan, Yarchaung, Ahtelthae, Hsininngyi, Yayphyukan and Chaungwa in Ponnagyun, and Aungseik, Thanchaung, Kalarchaung, Aungma, Magyichaung, Angumaw, Kyetyoeseik and Sarpyingyi in Rathedaung. Fighter jets and artillery also damaged the 450-year-old Gu Wa Pagoda in Ponnagyun, destroying many of its roughly 500 Arahat statues in the third such attack on the site. The clashes come as the AA maintains a siege of Sittwe from within roughly 2km, having already captured 14 of Rakhine's 17 townships.

media.caption: Residents flee Ponnagyun and Rathedaung townships as junta and Arakan Army forces exchange heavy artillery, MLRS and drone strikes near Sittwe.

title: Min Aung Hlaing Arrives in Hanoi for Three-Day Vietnam State Visit, Fourth ASEAN Trip Since Becoming President
detail: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing landed at Noi Bai International Airport in Hanoi at noon on September 4, 2026, beginning a three-day state visit at the invitation of Vietnamese President To Lam. The trip — his eighth foreign visit and third to an ASEAN member state since taking the civilian presidency in April 2026, following Laos (July) and Thailand (August 6-7) — included meetings with To Lam, Prime Minister Pham Minh Chinh and National Assembly Chairman Tran Thanh Man, plus a Myanmar-Vietnam business forum. Myanmar officials disclosed that bilateral trade has collapsed from $853 million in 2020 to $590 million in 2025 and just $335 million in the first half of 2026. The visit is part of Min Aung Hlaing's broader campaign to normalize Myanmar's standing within ASEAN; a further visit to Cambodia is planned for September 11-12.

media.caption: Min Aung Hlaing arrived in Hanoi September 4, 2026 for a three-day Vietnam state visit.
